review: 1:1–1:4 אָמֵן, בּוֹא — Revelation 22:20 (אָמֵן, בֹּאָה אֲדֹנֵינוּ יֵשׁוּעַ); the Arabic آمِينْ تَعَالَ يَا حَبِيبِي / آمِينْ تَعَالَ يَا يَسُوع is that prayer, and the Hebrew keeps the amen at the head of each line as the Arabic does.
2:1–2:2 הִנְנִי גֵר / בְּדַרְכִּי אֶל־בֵּיתִי — Psalm 39:13 with the pilgrimage image of 1 Peter 2:11; the Arabic إِنَّنِي غَرِيبٌ / فِي طَرِيقِي لِلدِّيَار is the same traveller.
3:2 לָקַחַת אֶת־עַמְּךָ — 'to take Your people'; the Arabic لِاخْتِطَافِ شَعْبِكَ is the rapture of 1 Thess 4:17, and לָקַחַת is the verb the New Testament uses for it.
3:3–3:4 לִבָּם … נִכְסָף / וְעֵינֵיהֶם אֵלֶיךָ — the Arabic splits heart and eyes across the couplet; Hebrew keeps the split so each line has its own subject.
